title: Python Programming Foundations Lab
summary: Build practical Python utilities covering variables, functions, data structures, file handling, and exceptions, then package them into a menu-driven command-line application.
problem: Many students begin AI and software development without strong programming fundamentals. Build a command-line toolkit for students and beginners with utilities such as unit conversion, expense calculation, text processing, grade calculation, and file management. Organize the code into reusable modules, validate inputs, handle errors, and test important functions. The project is complete when another developer can clone the repository, install its dependencies, run the menu-driven application, and understand each utility through documented examples. Include at least fifteen useful operations and demonstrate that invalid inputs do not crash the program.
submissionCriteria: README with installation and usage examples

title: Data Structures and Algorithms Practice Suite
summary: Implement arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, searching, and sorting algorithms with examples, tests, and complexity analysis.
problem: Technical interviews commonly assess problem-solving and data structures. Build a practice suite that teaches students how core structures work internally rather than relying only on built-in implementations. Implement linear structures, a binary search tree, and fundamental searching and sorting algorithms. Each implementation must include examples, edge cases, and time and space complexity notes. The finished repository should be useful for interview preparation and easy for other students to extend. Demonstrate correctness with automated tests and compare algorithm performance on multiple input sizes.
submissionCriteria: At least six data structure implementations
At least eight searching and sorting algorithms

title: Responsive Developer Portfolio Website
summary: Create a responsive portfolio featuring projects, skills, education, and contact details, with an optional AI-powered project-description assistant.
problem: Students need a professional online presence to showcase skills and projects when applying for internships and placements. Build a responsive portfolio presenting a profile, education, technical expertise, project demonstrations, achievements, and contact information. As an optional AI enhancement, connect a free-tier model through a backend endpoint to draft concise project descriptions from facts supplied by the student. The site must work on mobile, tablet, and desktop screens, load efficiently, and have a shareable public URL. Keep any model credentials on the server and never expose API keys in frontend code.

Include authentication, consistent error responses, pagination, API documentation, and automated tests. title: Email Spam Detection Classifier
summary: Train a text classifier that identifies spam using NLP preprocessing, TF-IDF features, and machine learning, then expose it through an application.

Compare at least two approaches and examine false positives and false negatives because incorrectly blocking a legitimate message can be costly. Provide an interface where users paste a message and receive a classification with an appropriate confidence indicator. title: AI-Powered Semantic Search Engine
summary: Develop semantic search that embeds documents, stores vectors in a vector index, and retrieves relevant passages by query meaning.
prerequisites: Understanding of JSON and REST APIs
problem: Keyword search can fail when a user's wording differs from the wording in source documents. Build a semantic search engine that retrieves relevant passages based on meaning. Ingest PDF, TXT, or Markdown files, split them into passages, generate embeddings using an open-source sentence transformer, and index vectors with FAISS. Users should submit natural-language queries and inspect matching passages with source names and similarity scores. Evaluate retrieval using a manually prepared query benchmark and compare it with a keyword baseline. Support index updates, malformed-document handling, and local inference without a paid embedding service.
